title: Store how a Cook wants to be addressed
objective: Add the column the gendered-strings sweep reads from. Arabic marks gender on the second person and there is no neutral form, so Kafoo either asks or guesses.
acceptance_criteria: a migration adds the column with RLS enabled in the same file
an authorization test proves a non-owner cannot WRITE another Cook's stored form, and was seen to FAIL before the policy existed
an authorization test proves the stored form is readable exactly where the Kitchen Profile already is — on an open kitchen and nowhere else
the field is optional, and every string still renders when it is unset
business-rules.md's privacy questions are answered in the migration comment: why it is needed, how long it is kept, who reads it
notes: Founder approved 2026-08-05, three decisions. (1) The column lives on kitchen_profiles and is therefore readable by anyone who can already see the kitchen, including anonymous visitors of an open kitchen — the deliberate exposure ADR-0010 anticipated for the two Customer-facing strings that describe a Cook. The original second criterion said a non-owner must not READ it, which contradicted the ADR; it was wrong and is now a write test plus an explicit read-scope test. (2) The Cook is asked during Kitchen Profile creation (T090, WP-007), so nothing guesses. The column stays nullable because that question does not exist until WP-007 lands, and ICU requires an `other` branch regardless; unset renders today's wording. (3) The migration comment answers business-rules.md's four privacy questions. Near auth and RLS, so it takes the expensive model. Shares supabase/tests/ with nothing currently open, but the plan(N) line at the top of each suite is a guaranteed conflict if a second package adds cases there.
